posts.quote: Me on Wednesday, after Monday and Tuesday took everything I had to give
posts.caption: By Wednesday morning I had already put the milk in the pantry and the cereal in the fridge. Nobody saw. I fixed it quietly and kept moving. At 10:40 I was in a meeting nodding along to a slide I had not read, writing notes with a pen that turned out to be a highlighter. Lunch was half a granola bar I found in my coat pocket, still wrapped, which I count as a win. There's still Thursday. Thursday has never once been kind to me, but it comes with the promise of Friday, so I show up.
posts.first: On Tuesday night I set up the coffee maker so Wednesday me would have a head start. Wednesday me found the filter in the pot and no coffee in it. I stood there holding the empty scoop like it owed me money. I made tea. Tea is what you make when you've lost.

posts.quote: You say people always take advantage of you ... how so?
posts.caption: I never saw the problem until my sister pointed it out. Last month she asked to borrow my good casserole dish, and I said of course. She still has it. Before that it was my ladder, a winter coat, and a Tuesday afternoon spent helping her move a couch she later decided against. I said yes to all of it. I also said yes when a neighbor asked me to water her tomatoes for a weekend in May. It's October and I'm still on tomato duty. The plants have been gone since July. I water the pots anyway.
posts.first: My sister called last night to ask if I could pick up her dry cleaning since I was already out. I wasn't out. I put my shoes on and got in the car anyway. The woman at the counter handed me four bags and said you must be the sister. I said I'm the one who does this. She nodded like she had heard it before.

posts.quote: Instead of wishing you were young again, just be glad you were young then.
posts.caption: I found the shoebox from 1994 on Sunday and made the mistake of opening it. There I was in a jacket with shoulder pads I could have landed a plane on, holding a perm that had clearly won a fight with me. I looked incredible. I did not know it then. At the time I was sure I was behind on everything, including my hair, my career and a cassette I'd promised to return. Turns out I was doing fine. I'd go back for an afternoon, but I'd leave the perm at home.
posts.first: I showed my husband the photo with the shoulder pads. He said wow and nothing else, which I've decided to take as awe. I put the box back on the closet shelf. By Tuesday I'll probably open it again. It's become a hobby, like driving past a house you used to live in.

posts.quote: I'm a true crime detective. Couch division; snacks unit. We're pretty sure the husband did it.
posts.caption: Episode three and I already had a theory, a bag of pretzels and a blanket fort of evidence. My husband came in to ask what I was watching, and I paused it on the guilty face. He looked at the screen. He looked at me. I told him it was a documentary about gardening. He asked why the woman in it was holding a shovel at two in the morning. I said that's what gardening is. He went to bed. Season two drops Friday. I've cleared my schedule and my snack cabinet.
posts.first: I told my husband last week I would solve the case before the finale. He said it was the neighbor. I said the neighbor doesn't even own a shovel. He said, exactly. I have notes now. Several pages of notes. He asked what they were for and I said I'm not at liberty to discuss it.

posts.quote: I've survived two mortgages and a kitchen remodel, and a fitted sheet still wins.
posts.first: I watched a video last week where a man folded one in four seconds. I tried it. I now own a very large, very wrinkled ball that lives on the top shelf of the linen closet with the others. We don't discuss them. It's a peaceful arrangement.

posts.quote: This morning I saw an envelope on my doorstep that said: ‘Do Not Bend’. I stood there for ages trying to figure out how to pick it up…
posts.caption: I stood there longer than I'd like to admit, and the mail carrier watched the entire thing from her truck. Eventually I sent my husband out in his socks. He handled it like a live animal, slid it onto a baking sheet, and carried it flat to the kitchen table like a tray of cupcakes. We opened it together. It was a coupon for a free oil change that expired in September. I want it noted that nobody bent.
posts.first: The carrier honked as she pulled away, and I'd like to believe it was congratulations. I took the baking sheet back inside. It's still on the counter. Nobody has moved it, and I think we're all waiting to see who goes first.

posts.quote: This isn't a secret passage, either. It's just another closet filled with plastic bags.
posts.caption: There is a closet in my house I've been afraid of since the spring. It started with one bag of bags. Then the bag of bags had a bag of bags. Last Saturday my husband opened the door looking for the vacuum and a wave of grocery bags rolled out like a tide. We both stood there. He asked how many there were. I said enough to carry every grocery I'll ever buy, which is the plan. He closed the door slowly, like a man leaving a museum. We still can't find the vacuum.
posts.first: I took four reusable bags to the store last week to be responsible, left them in the trunk, and bought a new bag at the register. The cashier asked if I wanted to keep it. I said I already have some. She didn't ask anything else.

posts.quote: My broom runs on farts; it is the only gas I can afford!
posts.caption: I priced gas on the way to work Monday and thought seriously about walking. Watching those pump numbers climb turned my commute into a quiet conversation with myself. Then I started adding up everything else: groceries, the heating bill, the dog's special food, which he doesn't even like. I've started wearing a sweater in the house and calling it a lifestyle. My husband turned the thermostat down two degrees and told me it builds character. I said I have plenty. He moved it back up. He's learning.
posts.first: Yesterday I carpooled and told everyone it was for the planet. The planet had nothing to do with it. My coworker brought a thermos and a bag of mints and I would like to move in with her. We're splitting gas on Fridays and sharing a heated seat. It's going well.

posts.quote: “Do you have a minute?” is the scariest question at work. Nobody has ever needed just one.
posts.first: Last Thursday a coworker asked if I had a minute at 4:52 p.m. I said of course, because I have no instinct for self-defense. At 5:40 I was still standing by her desk holding my coat. We resolved nothing. She thanked me for my time like it was a donation.

posts.quote: When I finally snap, it is going to be because I had to type my email address with my TV remote.
posts.caption: I know exactly which streaming service did this to me. It wanted an email, then a password with a capital, a number and a symbol I have never used in my life. It's one letter at a time across a keyboard on the screen, with the cursor jumping around like it's nervous. I got as far as the at sign and the app timed out. I started over. My husband walked in, saw my face, and slowly backed out of the room. The show I wanted to watch is twenty-two minutes long.
posts.first: I finally said my email out loud to the television like it could hear me. It did not. My husband offered to set it up on his phone in two minutes. I said I would rather finish it by hand even if it takes until Easter. We're on week two.

posts.quote: “What do you do for work?” chug caffeine and hope for the f*cking best
posts.caption: At a party last month somebody asked me what I do and I gave them my title. They nodded. Then they asked what I actually do, and I think that was the honest question. So I told them. I answer emails that answer other emails, I sit in rooms where we agree to meet again, and I keep a drawer of snacks that has saved at least three careers. They said that sounds stressful. I said only on days that end in y. I asked what they do. They're an accountant. We both finished our drinks very fast.
posts.first: My mug at the office says World's Okayest Employee. A coworker gave it to me as a joke in 2019. I've used it every single day since, and nobody has ever offered to replace it, so I think I got the right one.

posts.quote: I invented a new drink. Prune juice and tequila. I call it “SHITS AND GIGGLES”
posts.caption: My sister brought a jug of prune juice to Sunday dinner like it was a gift. She said it was for regularity, and I said this is a family dinner. My brother-in-law added that he'd heard it was good for you. Everyone nodded. Nobody drank any. The jug sat in the middle of the table next to the green bean casserole like a guest nobody invited, slowly gathering a small audience of glances. She left it when she went home. It's in my fridge now. It keeps looking at me.
posts.first: I found the jug behind the milk this morning. I've decided it's a decorative item now. My husband asked if I was going to use it. I said I'm thinking about it, which is also what I say about gym memberships and the shed.
